title: Annotatio III §.VI (3): Frankfurt Estates (third year after) approve the Leipzig Colloquy and decree Saxony and Brandenburg continue the Protestant peace work
pass_a_gloss: Finally (3.) that the Estates of the Empire, gathered at Frankfurt on the Main in the third year afterward, not only approved the Leipzig Colloquy, but judging that they would scarcely be frustrated of the Hope of the Leipzig Theologians, sanctioned by a peculiar Decree that the Most Serene Electors, the Saxon and the Brandenburg, were to be asked in their public name, that they should care that the Business of Protestant Peace, begun at Leipzig, be continued by the labor of several more moderate Theologians, and be led through to a happy outcome. The Decree of the Estates, since it has come to the knowledge of few, we exhibit here to our Reader, in those words in which we read it described in John Dury’s Prodromus of Irenic Works, page 1.
pass_b_english: (3.) Finally, in the third year afterward the Imperial Estates gathered at Frankfurt am Main not only approved the Leipzig Colloquy, but — judging they would not be cheated of the Leipzig theologians’ hope — sanctioned by a special decree that Electors Saxony and Brandenburg be asked in the Estates’ public name to keep the Protestant peace business begun at Leipzig going through more moderate theologians’ work, and to bring it to a happy end.
Because few know that decree, we set it out here in the words printed in John Dury’s Prodromus Irenicorum, p. 1.
source_text: Denique (3.) quòd Status Imperii, tertio post anno, Francofurti ad Moenum congregati, non tantum Colloqv. Lipf. aprobarunt, sed Spe Theologorum Lipsiensium se haud frustratum iri arbitrati, Decreto peculiari sanciverunt, Electores Serenissimos, Saxonicum & Brandenburgicum, publico suo nomine rogandos esse, quò Pacis Protestanticae Negotium, Lipsiae inchoatum, plurium Theologorum moderatiorum operâ, continuandum, & ad felicem exitum perducendum curarent. Decretum Statuum, cùm ad paucorum notitiam pervenerit, exhibemus hic Lectori nostro, iis verbis, quibus illud in Joh. Durai Prodromo Irenicorum descriptum legimus, pag. 1.

lemmas.gloss: John Dury’s Prodromus of Irenic Works

notes: Lipsiacum (3): Frankfurt Estates decree; Duraeus Prodromus p.1 source for Decretum text.
